result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.intersection()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the intersection of this graph with another graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12119-L12185){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.intersection(other) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns a new graph containing only edges that exist in both graphs. Nodes are included only if they are endpoints of common edges. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The graph to intersect with. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph containing edges present in both graphs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graphs have different directedness. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - Both graphs must have the same directedness - Only edges present in both graphs are included - Nodes without edges are excluded - Uses this graph's edge weights/attributes ## Examples {.doc-examples} Only the edges present in both graphs survive -- here, both graphs share edges `1-2` and `2-3`, but the triangle's closing edge and the square's extra edges don't overlap: ::: {#c0a80476 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Triangle g1 = ec.Graph(directed=False) for i in range(1, 4): g1.add_node() g1.add_edge(1, 2) g1.add_edge(2, 3) g1.add_edge(3, 1) # Square with diagonal g2 = ec.Graph(directed=False) for i in range(1, 5): g2.add_node() g2.add_edge(1, 2) g2.add_edge(2, 3) g2.add_edge(3, 4) g2.add_edge(4, 1) common = g1.intersection(g2) common.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: This is useful for finding stable connections that exist at multiple time points or in multiple network versions.
